official.deadline_note: No fixed closing date: the official page states 'Applications /Nominations are open all around the year' (rolling submission).
official.application_cycle: Rolling; applications/nominations accepted all around the year
official.status_note: The page's Call Status field reads 'The call is currently open'; the fellowships overview page also lists it as currently open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published Terms of the Scholarships list only international low-cost airfare (borne by COMSTECH) and accommodation, subsistence, supervision and local training provided by the host institution; no tuition or enrolment fee coverage is stated anywhere on the page.

Age limit: maximum 35 years for graduate studies, 45 years for post-graduate studies
Preference is given to young scientists (particularly women scientists) at the beginning of their research career, and those working in Least Developed OIC Countries
requirements: Field: natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering and technology, with the placement hosted at a CCoE member institution
Applications can only be submitted through email to COMSTECH Headquarters, Islamabad, Pakistan (khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org)
Scanned copy of a valid passport, plus M.S./Ph.D. degrees and relevant university transcripts
CV of maximum five pages, including publications
Supporting statement from the head of the home institution
Two reference letters from senior scientists familiar with the applicant's work; the head of the home institution cannot be one of the referees

official.application_route: Email only: complete the official application form linked on the call page and send it with the full document set to khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org at COMSTECH Headquarters, Islamabad.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of a least developed country of the OIC, or employed by a research institution in an OIC country.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to general international applicants: eligibility is restricted to citizens of OIC least-developed countries or researchers employed by a research institution in an OIC country, with the placement hosted at a CCoE member institution in an OIC member state.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering and technology; the placement must be at a host institution that is a member of the COMSTECH Consortium of Excellence (CCoE).
official.research_requirement: The fellowships are for research and advanced training at a host centre of excellence; a supporting statement from the head of the home institution and two reference letters from senior scientists are required, but no separate research proposal is specified on the page.
official.duration: 6-12 months, extendable upon recommendation of the host institution
official.description: COMSTECH and prestigious CCoE member institutions jointly offer research fellowships to young researchers in OIC countries to enable them to spend 6-12 months at a relevant centre of excellence among the listed institutions of OIC member states. The purpose is to enhance the research and development capacity of promising researchers and engineers, especially those from LDCs at the beginning of their research career, helping them foster linkages for further collaboration in their fields.
official.region: Multiple (OIC member states; the call targets least-developed countries of the OIC)
official.program_type: Inter-governmental research fellowship for research and advanced training

verification.notes: Amount, currency and cadence are not published anywhere on the official page; it lists only what the award covers (airfare, accommodation, subsistence, supervision/mentoring) with no monetary figure, so those fields are null. Deadline is rolling ('open all around the year'), so no deadline date exists. The one-programme-per-calendar-year rule is published on COMSTECH's own fellowship terms page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a COMSTECH-run, 6-12 month research placement for citizens of OIC least-developed countries (or staff of OIC research institutions) in natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering or technology, hosted at Consortium of Excellence member institutions across OIC states. There is no closing date: submissions are accepted all year, so the real constraint is matching with a host institution rather than beating a deadline. COMSTECH pays only the international low-cost airfare, while accommodation and subsistence come from the host institution, meaning the value you receive depends heavily on which host accepts you. Everything arrives by email to the Islamabad secretariat, and selection is a joint merit decision by COMSTECH and the host's scholarship committee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career scientists and engineers (M.S. or Ph.D. holders, or active researchers) aged 35 or under in graduate studies - 45 or under post-graduate - from an OIC least-developed country who can secure six to twelve months away at a CCoE host lab.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the LDC list published with the call page, and shortlist CCoE member institutions whose labs match your field before writing anything

Contact a prospective host supervisor informally first - the host institution controls accommodation, subsistence and the extension recommendation, so a named acceptee weighs heavily with the joint committee

Draft the five-page CV strictly including the publications list, and ask the head of your home institution for the supporting statement early since you also need that person to be excluded from your referee choices
Line up two senior scientist referees who know your work and are not your institutional head

Assemble a single email containing the completed form, valid passport scan, five-page CV, supporting statement, two reference letters, and degree certificates with transcripts, sent to khazima@comstech.org and comstech@comstech.org
common_rejection_risks: Field mismatch: only natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering and technology qualify, and the placement must sit at a CCoE member institution
Choosing the head of your home institution as a referee, which the call explicitly forbids
Age over the 35-year (graduate) or 45-year (post-graduate) limit, since the published limits are applied per study category
A CV that runs past five pages, or missing university transcripts alongside the degree certificates
Applying to another COMSTECH programme in the same calendar year, which bars a second visit that year
No prior contact with a host institution, leaving the joint committee with no host willing to provide accommodation and mentorship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and related travel-document fees, any airfare above the 'low-cost' international economy fare COMSTECH covers, health insurance, personal expenses and dependants' costs, plus any tuition, bench or enrolment fees the host institution may charge (none are covered under the published terms). The subsistence standard itself is set by each host institution and is not published by COMSTECH.
document_audit: The passport scan must be from a VALID passport on this scheme (sibling COMSTECH fellowships accept expired copies, this call does not)
CV is capped at five pages including the publications list, so trim teaching and service content
Degrees AND transcripts are both required, not just certificates
The supporting statement must come from the head of the home institution, while that same person is disqualified as a referee
alerts: Rolling deadline is a trap in reverse: there is no closing rush, but also no advertised start date or intake calendar, so build in a long lead time between emailing the application and arriving at the host lab
COMSTECH publishes no monetary value for this fellowship; treat any stipend figure found on aggregator sites as unverified and ask the secretariat what subsistence the specific host provides
Only one COMSTECH programme application is permitted per calendar year, so applying for this alongside another COMSTECH fellowship disqualifies the second
Preference is explicitly biased toward women scientists and researchers working in least-developed OIC countries, so applicants outside those groups must make a stronger scientific-merit case
Extending beyond the initial term is possible only on the host institution's recommendation, not automatic
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online application form linked on the call page, attach the full document set, and email everything to khazima@comstech.org or comstech@comstech.org; COMSTECH and the host institution then review the file jointly and award on scientific merit.
